networkAccess.reasoning: Published, this plugin has no network access at all: allowedDomains stays "none". Run as a development plugin — the only way it is run — it opens one WebSocket to port 8791 on the loopback interface and to nothing else. That socket answers one question: the file's current local variables, in the shape Figma's own read endpoint returns them, so machinery/scripts/check-drift.mjs can compare this file against the token source on a plan where the variables REST API is closed. It carries no command that changes anything — the whole vocabulary is hello, snapshot-request, snapshot and error, with no word for create, update, rename or delete. It sends the variable table plus the document's name and key, so a drift report can say which file it read; never the canvas, never the document itself. Whatever holds that port is what answers, so this field does not claim anybody in particular started it.
